correctness.rationale: On each active planar skew oscillator the modified Heun update is ((1-br_j)I+hω_j J)u_j with b=1/2−ε. Orthogonality yields gain (1-br_j)^2+r_j; conservation is V b²−2U b+U=0, real roots iff μ=V/U<=1, both b>=1/2. Substituting 1−2b=−b²μ gives gain 1+b²r_j(r_j−μ). If r*<=1 then μ<=r* at every state so roots always exist. If r*>1 every feasible step multiplies the maximal active frequency group by at least 1+δ, δ=r*(r*−1)/4>0, contradicting finite conserved total energy after more than floor(log(E_total/E*,0)/log(1+δ)) steps; no branch switching avoids this. For two active modes a<1<c the initial μ<=1 inequality is exactly p<=a(1−a)/[a(1−a)+c(c−1)]. Independent exact rational computation checked the example r=(1/4,9/4), initial E=(27,1), b=2/3, next E=(51/2,5/2), U1=12,V1=57/4, next discriminant=-108.
